Achievement: 🔴 RED (30%)

Evidence & Status:
- v15 dataset: ~5M pairs (code_edits 32%, single_file 24.3%, diff_gen 16.2%) [supporting-docs/V15_FINAL_DATASET_SUMMARY.md]
- v16.2 dataset: ~8M pairs (governance/constraint scenarios) [supporting-docs/V17_DATASET_SUMMARY.md comparison section]
- v17 dataset: ~2M pairs (2,411 examples, 217 files, 29 packages, 100% real Motadata) [supporting-docs/V17_DATASET_SUMMARY.md]
- Total: ~15M pairs (15% of 100M target); uncertain utility (10-30% may be repurposed; remainder is learning tax)
- Benchmark: 50 scenarios designed, not operationalized

Why Behind (30% vs 100%):
Strategic pivot mid-Q3 from high-volume commodity pairs to golden exemplars with reasoning DNA [supporting-docs/EXEMPLAR_AUTHORING_GUIDE.md]. 
Critical realization: QLORA on v15/v16.2/v17 trains helpfulness without judgmental reasoning (shows "what to do" not "how to think"). 
Better approach: 30 manually-curated golden exemplars → 25K+ reasoning-embedded variants (250+ per exemplar) = same volume, exponentially better behavioral quality.

What We Got Instead:
- Golden exemplar framework [supporting-docs/EXEMPLAR_AUTHORING_GUIDE.md, supporting-docs/Golden_Exemplars.mp4]
- 7-category taxonomy (RCA, Anomaly, Refusal, Constraint, Design, MultiLayer, Coding) [supporting-docs/EXEMPLAR_AUTHORING_GUIDE.md]
- 9 review criteria + 3 D.N.A validation gates [supporting-docs/EXEMPLAR_AUTHORING_GUIDE.md]
- 5/30 exemplars locked (Phase-1 foundation)
- Variant generation strategy (250+ per exemplar)

Forward Path:
- Feb 05: Lock 30/30 exemplars (manual, critical)
- Mid-Feb: Generate 25K+ variants (semi-automated)
- End-Feb: Build SFT dataset (automated)

Summary:
Technically RED (missed volume target). Strategically sound—traded volume for depth. Pivot is intentional, model-agnostic, and improves long-term robustness. 6 weeks behind but targeting exponentially higher behavioral quality.

column4: Achieve > 40% accuracy and 20% hallucination reduction on benchmark
column5:
Success Criteria
[ ] >40% accuracy achieved
[ ] 20% hallucination reduction measured
[ ] Prototype model ready
column6:
Achievement: 🔴 RED (25%)

Evidence & Status:
- Baseline metrics collected for 12 coding tasks: logic 0.541, entity extraction 0.40, hallucination 1.00 [supporting-docs/BASELINE_EVALUATION_RESULTS.md]
- v16.2 deployed Jan 7, marked broken Jan 8 (ignores RAG, contradicts itself), rolled back [supporting-docs/MODEL_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md]
- v15/v16.2/v17 datasets (~15M pairs) exist but lack reasoning DNA [supporting-docs/V15_FINAL_DATASET_SUMMARY.md, supporting-docs/V17_DATASET_SUMMARY.md]
- QLORA infra ready [supporting-docs/TRAINING_MONITOR.md]; no SFT run yet

Why Behind (25% vs 100%):
1. Baseline incomplete: 12 coding tasks done; need expanded AIOps scenarios (RCA, anomaly, refusal, constraint, design, config, coding)
2. Golden exemplar dataset not ready: 5/30 exemplars locked; QLORA on commodity pairs trains helpfulness without safety/reasoning [supporting-docs/EXEMPLAR_AUTHORING_GUIDE.md]
3. No SFT iteration: Waiting for reasoning-embedded variants (250+ per exemplar) to avoid behavioral regression

Root Cause:
Strategic pivot from high-volume commodity pairs to golden exemplars with embedded reasoning DNA [supporting-docs/EXEMPLAR_AUTHORING_GUIDE.md, supporting-docs/From_Fluency_to_Judgment.mp4]. QLORA on v15/v16.2/v17 alone would achieve >40% task accuracy but with unsafe defaults ("be helpful" not "think first"). New path: teach HOW to think (decompose, validate, detect adversarial patterns) BEFORE WHAT to do, targeting >70% accuracy + 30% hallucination reduction with safe behavioral defaults.

Forward Path:
- Feb 05: Lock 30/30 exemplars (manual, critical)
- Mid-Feb: Generate variants (semi-automated)
- End-Feb/Early-Mar: Build SFT dataset and train QLORA (automated)
- Mid-Mar: Benchmark and measure post-SFT metrics

Summary:
Deliberate trade-off: later but safer. Aiming for robust behavioral defaults over quick unsafe gains. Industry precedent: Bloomberg, Google, Tabnine use similar golden exemplar approaches [cited in EXEMPLAR_AUTHORING_GUIDE.md case studies].
